committee_name.text: Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee (DODAC)

quote.quote: The application for Eylea (aflibercept) was presented to the Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee (DODAC) on June 17, 2011.
The Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee of the Food and Drug Administration met on June 17, 2011.

recommendation.text: The committee voted unanimously 10 to 0 that aflibercept demonstrated efficacy and safety in neovascular AMD, and recommended the 2 mg every 8 weeks regimen (after 3 monthly loading doses).

quote.quote: The committee voted unanimously (10 Yes; 0 No) that the product demonstrated efficacy and safety in neovascular AMD, and recommended the 2 mg every 8 weeks dosing regimen (after 3 loading doses given every 4 weeks).

linkages.concern: The committee recommended the 2 mg every 8 weeks (Q8) regimen (after 3 monthly loading doses), rather than the other dosing/formulation options in the original application.
linkages.change: Regeneron amended the BLA to withdraw the other dose/formulation, and the product was approved at 2 mg every 8 weeks (following 3 initial monthly doses).

concern_quote.quote: The committee recommended 2mg every eight weeks (Q8) with an extra dose at month 2 (2mg monthly for 3 months then once every 2 months).

change_quote.quote: However, based on recommendations from the Advisory Committee and Division that the 2 mg dose (40 mg/mL formulation) given every 8 weeks was effective and provided patients with the advantage of less frequent intravitreal injections, Regeneron decided to send an amendment (b) (4) from the BLA on August 1, 2011.

linkages.concern: There was discussion that information on injections every 4 weeks should be included in labeling to allow flexibility for scheduling return appointments.
linkages.change: The approved labeling states dosing can be given as frequently as every 4 weeks.

concern_quote.quote: There was discussion that information on injections every 4 weeks could be included in labeling to allow flexibility for scheduling return appointments.

change_quote.quote: Dosing can be given as frequently as every 4 weeks based on the results of both Phase 3 studies, but no added benefit was seen with more frequent dosing.

linkages.concern: The committee commented on including information on increased intraocular pressure (IOP) in labeling.
linkages.change: The labeling reflects increased intraocular pressure as a reported adverse reaction.

concern_quote.quote: including information on increased IOP in labeling

change_quote.quote: The labeling will reflect findings of nasal ulcerations seen in monkey studies, and adverse reactions reported during clinical trials: arterial thrombotic events, increased intraocular pressure, immunogenicity, and rare complications of intravitreal injections such as endophthalmitis and retinal detachment.

summary: The Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee (DODAC) met June 17, 2011 and voted unanimously (10-0) that aflibercept demonstrated efficacy and safety in neovascular AMD, specifically recommending the 2 mg every-8-weeks regimen (after 3 monthly loading doses). Following the committee's and Division's recommendation of the 2 mg Q8 regimen, Regeneron amended the BLA to withdraw the other dose/formulation, and the product was approved on that regimen. The committee also discussed labeling points (every-4-week dosing flexibility and inclusion of increased IOP information) that are reflected in the approved labeling, though the review documents do not explicitly tie those labeling choices to the committee.
